 Show Most recent Most popular Managers won't 'touch Man Utd at the moment ' published at 16:33 GMT 16:33 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Paul Robinson 
Former Leeds goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 On whether Michael Carrick will still be manager by their next game: 
 I can't answer that honestly, I really don't know because of how the club is. I think there's so many different options. 
 The club could decide to go in a different direction and Michael Carrick, who would blame him if he turned around and went in a different direction. 
 To give you my opinion, I don't think he will be, but for whichever reason I don't know. 
 But then from Manchester United's perspective, who do you get? What do you want? Because Unai Emery's not coming and who wants to be in control of this football club? No-one would touch them at the moment and the way the club is and the structure of it.

 Post published at 16:33 GMT 16:33 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 All very scrappy early on and Leeds wing-back Jayden Bogle sums it up with a a shot dragged well wide.
 9 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'What's next I really don't know' published at 16:31 GMT 16:31 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, speaking to Sky Sports: "Leny [Yoro] slipped for one goal, it was a dubious free-kick against Ayden [Heaven] for another.
 "I didn't think anyone was close enough to him for it to be a free-kick. Leny's slip is unfortunate, he's got a huge future and he's a talented player. He's made a mistake today and he's feeling it but he shouldn't. Mistakes happen - it's not even a mistake it's just a slip.
 "The third goal, the fans were there waiting for us to get something in the game second half if we'd got one chance, one goal in the second half they would have been with us. We just couldn't find that moment and that third goal is a killer moment. From that time it was what it was.
 "It's obvious to say that - strange mixed emotions of a finish of a game. Not a nice way to end the game."
 On players: "Tough day for them - we went into the game being rocked a bit and you could feel that on the pitch. They kept going and they're disappointed, they're hurt. The players are feeling it. It's not a nice feeling when you see the disappointment. It is what it is, you have to accept it and that's the situation we're in at the moment.
 "It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion - the dynamic of what it was like today. Not for me personally but for Man Utd. It was really mixed today. I feel a lot of responsibility, I've been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful to to see us going through this at this moment in time."
 On leaving Fernandes on the bench: "There's always times when you're trying to make decisions that are to change the course of play and made a difference but those are the decisions we made today."
 On lap of pitch at full-time: "It wasn't a farewell from me. I'm mixed emotions, I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment. Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way.
 "To have that connection with the supporters it's mixed emotions, it'll take a bit of time to digest but I certainly appreciate their support. The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough.
 "It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I will always do my best for the football club and I won't change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility - we'll have to wait and see."

 Brobbey is a huge plus for Sunderland published at 16:30 GMT 16:30 GMT 
 Sunderland v Leeds (16:30 GMT) 
 Gary Bennett 
Ex-Sunderland defender on BBC Radio Newcastle 
 Calvert-Lewin is a good player, we know that but I think we've got to look on the positive side as well.
 The biggest concern for Sunderland was Brobbey, and he is fit and if he plays to his strength, he will cause them problems. 
 We've got to look at that as a bonus because since the Manchester City game, he's been missed. Now hopefully he can hit the ground running again, and he's a huge plus for Sunderland.

 Calvert-Lewin fitness a boost for Leeds published at 16:29 GMT 16:29 GMT 
 Sunderland v Leeds (16:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin was a big doubt for this with a bruised foot so it's a huge boost for Leeds that he's been passed fit.
 Since November 29th last year, only Erling Haaland (21) has more Premier League goals than the Leeds striker (17), while the Englishman has the best conversion rate of the 52 players to have 40+ shots in that time (24.6%).

 Team news published at 16:28 GMT 16:28 GMT 
 Sunderland v Leeds (16:30 BST) 
 Right, we'll continue to bring you reaction to that humbling defeat for Manchester United at home to Bournemouth and what it means for Michael Carrick's future.
 But, of course, we have a big game in the north east to enjoy as well. The teams are out at the Stadium of Light and here's a reminder of how we expect them to line up.
 Both sides are buoyed by the inclusion of their big front men.

 Post published at 16:25 GMT 16:25 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Jamie Carragher 
Former Liverpool defender on Sky Sports 
 I don't think Michael Carrick was ever going to bring Bruno Fernandes on. I think it was a deliberate decision just to leave him on the bench and almost try to embarrass him a little bit in front of the supporters - I don't know.
 I think what Bruno did after the game in Como was on the back of him getting brought off and I think Michael Carrick never had any intention of bringing him on at all - that sub was never going to happen.

 Man Utd fans 'are getting fed up with it' published at 16:23 GMT 16:23 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Clinton Morrison 
Former Crystal Palace striker on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Fernandes went and warmed up [during the game] and usually he'd get a big round of applause but there was just a little round of applause with some of the fans singing 'Bruno, Bruno'. 
 I was surprised, I thought there'd be more behind him but they weren't behind him, so I think a lot of the fans probably agreed with it and are getting fed up with it.

 Post published at 16:22 GMT 16:22 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Ashley Young 
Former Man Utd winger on Sky Sports 
 There have been different managers [in recent seasons] but it's the same players. There have been a few changes in players but they're just not showing anything.
 You could tell today that it was like they'd given up - they're not running for this manager and they're not wanting to fight.
 The fans deserve so much more, you can tell they want more and they know he's been let down by those players.

 Post published at 16:20 GMT 16:20 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Something needs to change, says Harry Maguire. I think we're all thinking the same thing when it comes to what we expect that to be.
 Michael Carrick wore the face of a man who knew that, too, as he walked off at the end.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 244 92 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Something needs to change' published at 16:19 GMT 16:19 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Manchester United 
 Manchester United captain Harry Maguire speaking to Sky Sports: "It wasn't good enough. Disappointed to give a goal away so early - another set play - and conceding first in the Premier League it makes it difficult.
 "A mistake for the second makes it hard for ourselves. We didn't perform well enough as individuals or as a team and we didn't deserve anything from the game.
 "It's not clicking at the moment. Results are not good enough and performances in the last week not good enough. Still early in the season.
 "Got to find something, question yourself, look in the mirror - that's the most important thing - think what you can do more and what more you can contribute to the team and if we do that we'll get somewhere."
 Feel responsibility? "Of course - you have to look after your own performances and take responsibility. This is a huge club and every day you have to prove why you're wearing this badge.
 "At the moment we're not doing enough as players. Michael [Carrick] turned our season on its head last year and we played brilliant football and got brilliant results. This season we haven't performed well enough as individuals."
 Conversation in player group? "If those conversations happen it will remain private. We want to do more be better and get better results. At the moment it's nowhere near good enough and something needs to change."

 A tricky time for Leeds published at 16:18 GMT 16:18 GMT 
 Sunderland v Leeds (16:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images A quick reminder among the fall out to another damaging defeat for Manchester United that there is another game to come this afternoon as Sunderland host Leeds at the Stadium of Light.
 Leeds have never won a Premier League game in the 4:30pm kick-off slot in eight attempts (D3 L5).
 In the past two seasons, 49% of Leeds’ points in the Premier League have come in games kicking off at 8pm or later (28/57), which is 21% higher than any other ever-present team (Liverpool, 28%).

 Post published at 16:17 GMT 16:17 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Manchester United have failed to win in their last six games in the Premier League, their last longer winless streak was from 1 April 2025 to 16 May 2025, a run of eight games.
 202 37 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Carrick knows writing is on the wall' published at 16:16 GMT 16:16 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Ashley Young 
Former Man Utd winger on Sky Sports 
 Players have got to stand up and be counted, but then of course you're going to look at Ineos for what they did over the summer. They haven't recruited the best and they haven't got the players in.
 As players, there's no togetherness, there's individuals. They were all separated on the pitch and Bournemouth looked like the team that were on fire.
 It's disappointing to see Michael Carrick like that. I wish there were players who knew and had the love for the club that he's got.
 The players might look dejected, but I think Michael knows that the writing is on the wall.
 492 49 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:14 GMT 16:14 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Jamie Carragher 
Former Liverpool defender on Sky Sports 
 Manchester United need to make that [managerial] change tonight, they need to make that decision.
 The fans have taken the side of Michael Carrick and it's not about him being the manager, it's about him being a huge figure in United's history.
 Those players have done nothing compared to teams of the past so Michael Carrick is always going to win that fight with Bruno Fernandes, and rightly so, no matter how talented a player he is.
 But also, Manchester United as a football club, one of the biggest in the world, are 16th in the Premier League right now and that can't continue. Michael Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties tonight - not just for the good of Manchester United, but also for the good of Michael Carrick.
 It's not nice watching him walking around the stadium at the end, he's really hurting and what's happening right now is not good for United and not good for Carrick.
 692 292 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:13 GMT 16:13 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Manchester United have won just seven points from eight Premier League games this season (W1 D4 L3), their lowest at this stage of a league season since 1986-87 (4).
 This was their heaviest defeat at Old Trafford since December 2024, also against Bournemouth.
 340 45 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Managers living in Ferguson's shadow' published at 16:11 GMT 16:11 GMT 
 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Clinton Morrison 
Former Crystal Palace striker on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Every other manager has struggled apart from Sir Alex Ferguson at this football club and I still feel like when it comes to Man Utd, everyone is living in his shadow and not putting in managers and players nowhere near good enough. 
 But that starts from the top as well because I don't think their recruitment has been anywhere near good enough and that's on years gone by.

 FT: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth 
 Image source, Getty Images No sign of any players or Michael Carrick just yet but we'll bring you reaction from the Manchester United camp as soon as we have it.

 Liverpool took their chances and deserved their win. This Liverpool team, it takes take and we have a long way to go. You can see where Iraola will want this team to go. They will become a top team in the future.
